Ana: Quick sync — I ran a batch of fairness simulations for the microcommit tiers vs our surge / soft-slab policies. Results are noisy but show a consistent skew: smaller customers hit hard caps more often and experience disproportionate throttling. Need a decision on mitigation before next sprint.
Sam: Can you drop the sim config + load profile?
Ana: Pasted below. Synthetic mix: 70% small bursts (<5 qps), 20% medium steady, 10% heavy long tail. Policy variants: A) current softcap=80% with burst credits, B) probabilistic throttling at 90% with fairness-weight=0.6, C) dynamic backfill credits for small customers.
Ana: ```
profile: microcommit_fairness_v1
clients: 10k
mix: {small:0.7, medium:0.2, heavy:0.1}
variant_A: {softcap:0.8,credits:burst}
variant_B: {prob_throttle:0.9,fairness_w:0.6}
variant_C: {backfill_window:10m,credits:scaled_by_rps}
```
Jules: Interesting. Metrics?
Ana: TL;DR: A reduces cost for us but increases 95p latency for small customers by ~14%. B reduces tail latency but increases failed requests for heavy tenants (fallbacks to queued). C is best for fairness but increases unit cost ~8%. Full CSV attached to the thread (sim link: https://internal/sim/4765).
Mike: My worry is gating C — cost hit on Dedicated pilot customers might break SLA commitments. Are backfill credits opt-in?
Ana: We simulated both opt-in and default-on. Opt-in leaves current unfairness. Default-on meets fairness but increases cost.
Kat: Proposal: roll out C as opt-in for Dedicated + enterprise pilot, default to B for self-serve. Revisit after 2 weeks with metrics.
Sam: Implementation complexity? B is low (single throttler param). C needs per-customer accounting + billing tie-in.
Jules: Also consider a hybrid: C for Tier-1 customers flagged in billing, B for others. That reduces engineering surface.
Ana: @pricing-bot can you run quick calc for unit economics: average cost delta for C at 10% adoption across regions?
pricing-bot: calc queued. Estimated delta: +7.9% overall unit cost at 10% adoption, +12.4% at 25% adoption. (assumptions: median seq_len 64, avg token/sec 8).
Mike: +7.9% within runway for pilot if we flag pilot customers and charge a small premium or move to reserved commit.
Kat: For launch criteria: require (1) <5% regressed 95p latency for non-opted users, (2) observability in Console per-customer, (3) billing flag + notice. Agree?
Sam: Dev plan: B first (1 sprint), data plumbing for C (billing, console) next sprint. Need sign-off on commit to add the extra cost to pilot contracts.
Jules: Customer ops: prepare comms for pilot customers about expected changes and opt-in flow.
Ana: Decision check: Kat + Mike approve pilot path (C opt-in for enterprise) + global default to B for self-serve. Sam to implement B this sprint.
Kat: Approve :thumbsup:
Mike: Approve :thumbsup:
Sam: Acknowledged. Starting a PR for B's throttler param, will tag reviewers.
Ana: I'll draft the pilot contract language and a short runbook for the support team.
Jules: Add an alert in Console for conversion rate of credit usage — want to catch runaway cost.
Ana: Noted. Thanks all.
